1gfiybi:218: Behind the exponential TTL strategy is a deep information-theoretic intuition: the "certainty" of a data point increases monotonically over time. The probability distribution of late-arriving data approximately follows exponential decay—data delayed by 1 minute still has a non-negligible probability of being corrected, while data delayed by 30 minutes is almost certainly final. Aligning TTL with this probability distribution makes the cache's "staleness risk" approximately uniform across time buckets, rather than concentrated in the most recent bucket. This design is superior to a fixed TTL: a fixed TTL is either too short (wasting the cache value of historical data) or too long (making fresh data excessively stale).
